ถนนสายนี้ไม่ได้ถูกสร้างขึ้นเป็นแหล่งท่อง: This street was not originally created as a tourist attraction. It grew within Takua Pa old town, a port and water-trade center that later prospered during the tin-mining era. Chinese people from mainland China, Penang, and Singapore came to trade and mine, and shophouses, shops, hotels, coffee shops, and service businesses lined Thanon Udom Thara and Thanon Si Takua Pa.
อาคารสองฝั่งถนนจึงเป็นหลักฐานของเมืองพหุ: The buildings on both sides of the street are therefore evidence of a multicultural town, including Chinese-style shophouses and colonial-influenced buildings linked to the Baba community. The street served as the town's commercial and residential spine, not as the pedestrian street it is today.
เมื่อโครงการถนนคนเดินเริ่มขึ้นใน พ.ศ. 25: When the walking-street project began in 2007 (B.E. 2550), through cooperation among the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT), Phang Nga Office, Takua Pa Town Municipality, Talat Yai Community, and Senanuch Rangsan Community, the original street was turned into a public space for telling its history and reviving the community economy under the name “Takua Pa Old Town: Telling the Past”.

หลังบริษัทเหมืองแร่ปิดตัวและแร่ดีบุกลดลง: After mining companies closed and tin production declined, the economy of Takua Pa's old commercial district stagnated. Some buildings remained in good condition, while others deteriorated over time. Area studies indicate that the cultural street uses stories, food, local knowledge, and existing architecture as assets to bring people and income back to the district.
ชื่อโครงการเปลี่ยนจาก “ตะกั่วป่า เมืองเก: The project name later changed from “Takua Pa Old Town: Telling the Past” to “Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street”. The Department of Internal Trade's market registry gives 17 December 2017 (B.E. 2560) as the establishment/promotional date, while news sources place the start of activities in 2007 (B.E. 2550). These should therefore be understood as separate milestones: the start of activities and the market's registration/promotion.
ใน พ.ศ. 2565 จังหวัดและท้องถิ่นยังจัดกิจ: In 2022 (B.E. 2565), the province and local authorities were still holding green-season activities and offering free rides on pho thong trucks. This shows that the street was being used to distribute income and draw people back to the old district. No specific evidence was found that the entire street was damaged by the 2004 tsunami or that the entire street was registered as an ancient monument.

ข้อมูลทะเบียนตลาดของกรมการค้าภายในระบุว่: The Department of Internal Trade's market registry states that Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street is on Thanon Si Takua Pa and Thanon Udom Thara. It opens on Sundays from 14.00·20.00 and activities are free to visit. The information identifies an administrator at the market-system level, but does not name a separate legal entity responsible for the street.
ปัจจุบันถนนยังทำหน้าที่เป็นตลาดและพื้นที: Today, the street still serves as a market and community learning space, with local food and sweets, basketry, handicrafts, performances, Baba dress, photo exhibitions, and street art. The old Sino-Portuguese buildings remain the main setting for activities. Some are well preserved, while others show signs of deterioration over time. No announcement of a major restoration project specifically for this street was found in the sources checked.
ข่าวย้อนหลังยืนยันการจัดงานต่อเนื่องอย่า: Archived news confirms that events continued at least in 2022 (B.E. 2565), with community activities on the street in 2024 (B.E. 2567). It can therefore be concluded that the street is still used as a cultural market and activity space for local people. Actual opening hours may change by season or according to the organizer's announcements.

หลักฐานออนไลน์ที่เปิดอ่านได้ยังไม่ระบุว่: The available online evidence does not yet state when the open-air market was first built, who built it, or which project it began as. It is therefore not yet possible to responsibly say that this place originated in the tin-mining era, the era of the provincial rulers, or the period of modern urban expansion.
บริบทของตะกั่วป่าช่วยบอกได้เพียงว่าเมือง: Takua Pa's context only tells us that the town has roots in trade and mining, and that the market district is an important community area. There is still no direct evidence linking this food center to a specific role in the town during those periods. Replacing the site's history with the history of the old town therefore risks creating a story that goes beyond the sources.
แหล่งรีวิวอาหารที่เผยแพร่ในปี 2563 ระบุร: A food-review source published in 2020 (B.E. 2563) identifies Ko Ek's shop as being “in Takua Pa Open-Air Market” and records it as open during the daytime. This confirms that the area was already functioning as a market with food shops at that time, not merely as an empty lot.
ในปี 2567 เทศบาลเมืองตะกั่วป่าประชาสัมพั: In 2024 (B.E. 2567), Takua Pa Town Municipality promoted the open-air market as a center for many types of food, from rice with curry, made-to-order dishes, noodles, and khanom chin to snacks and drinks. A 2025 news report discusses plans to develop it into a modern food center or food court. This is a development plan, not evidence that construction was completed. No evidence has been found that the market was affected by the 2004 tsunami, abandoned, or registered as an ancient monument.
หลักฐานล่าสุดที่พบยืนยันการมีอยู่ของตลาด: The latest evidence found confirms the existence of the open-air market in 2024·2025 (B.E. 2567·2568) and shows that small vendors still use the space to sell food. The municipality once gave approximate opening hours of 08.00·22.00, but a review platform gives another set of hours, so the current schedule should not be considered verified.
ยังไม่พบประกาศปี 2569 ที่ยืนยันผู้ดูแลโด: No 2026 (B.E. 2569) announcement has yet been found confirming the direct administrator, building condition, facilities, or opening to visitors as a tourist attraction. There is also no confirming evidence that the plan to upgrade it into a modern food center/food court has been completed. The safest overall description is that it is a food market used by the community and small vendors, with a development direction, while current details should still be checked again with the municipality.
